mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% annualized over the past month signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL increases do not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE drops do not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansionary demand periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past month signals increased economic activity and supply-side strength, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increases do not correlate with subsequent economic activity improvements.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% annualized over the past month, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL > 2% annualized increase in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the past month, the combination signals a very tight labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of low UNRATE and high PAYEMS does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in the past two months signals strong demand in the housing sector, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially in a low-interest-rate environment.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increases do not correlate with subsequent improvements in the housing sector.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is increasing and real GDP (GDPC1) is growing at a rate above 2% annually, the combination signals robust economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increasing and GDPC1 growth > 2% annually
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of increasing INDPRO and high GDPC1 growth does not correlate with subsequent economic growth.
